blinding: Second-round packet-based re-adjudication. No author gold/rationale files read, but the change message disclosed that the five new technical-behavior claims were intended as insufficient; this round is not fully blind to their intended category. All five were independently checked against the packet.
evidence_convention: Minimal proof sets exclude optional corroboration. Insufficient requires evidence=[] and has no decisive proof set.

records.claim: Calling empty_cache while tensors are still live releases the GPU memory occupied by those tensors for another process.
records.label: contradicted
records.reason: D2 explicitly says occupied tensor memory is not freed; only unused cache is released.

ambiguities: Driver/plugin setup is an assumed premise; D1 is optional. This does not guarantee a runnable Pod, and D1 actually says to run the plugin.
records.claim: For our proposed container, after the vendor driver and device plugin are installed, a GPU limit can be specified without an explicit GPU request; Kubernetes uses that limit as the request.
records.label: supported
records.reason: D2 directly permits limits without requests and gives the default request value.

ambiguities: D3 defines type but need not be mandatory; D4 permits count changes, not type inconsistency.
records.claim: For our proposed typed-GPU allocation, the job step should request GPUs of that same type.
records.label: supported
records.reason: D1 explicitly requires matching GPU type between allocation and job step.

ambiguities: Shared prefix is now a premise; D1 is optional mechanism context, not required proof.
records.claim: For a request that shares an existing prefix, the documented APC benefit targets prompt processing rather than generation of new tokens.
records.label: supported
records.reason: D3 directly distinguishes prefill benefits from lack of decoding-time benefits.

ambiguities: Do not import external Kubernetes resource-granularity knowledge. Equality does not itself prohibit matching fractional request and limit values.
records.claim: The described GPU device plugin allows a container to request half of a physical GPU through its custom resource field.
records.label: insufficient
records.missing_information: The device plugin/custom resource's permitted allocation granularity and fractional-resource semantics.
records.reason: The packet gives request/limit equality and defaulting rules but no integer-only or fractional-GPU rule.

records.claim: A submission using the --gpus option will be accepted even when select/cons_tres is not configured.
records.label: contradicted
records.reason: D3 says --gpu* requests without select/cons_tres are rejected.

ambiguities: D4 checkpoint terminology refers to shared-prefix state and does not establish cross-process persistence.
records.claim: APC keeps its cached prefix blocks available after a full server process restart.
records.label: insufficient
records.missing_information: A restart persistence or restoration guarantee for APC prefix-cache blocks.
records.reason: Caching/reuse of existing queries does not specify persistence across a full process restart.

ambiguities: D1 is optional logical/admission-control context.
records.claim: Our proposed Ray task declaring num_cpus=1 is prevented by Ray from launching threads that use multiple physical CPUs.
records.label: contradicted
records.reason: D2 explicitly says Ray does not prevent num_cpus=1 work from using multiple physical CPUs.

ambiguities: D1 alone states an if-shared condition; do not require its converse when D3 provides the explicit negative.
records.claim: Enabling APC lets a request with no prefix in common with existing queries reuse their prefix computations.
records.label: contradicted
records.reason: D3 expressly says no shared prefix means the computation cannot be reused.

ambiguities: This is scheduling admission, not a physical CPU-use ceiling.
records.claim: Starting a head node with zero logical CPUs can prevent CPU-requiring work from being scheduled there even when the machine has physical CPUs.
records.label: supported
records.reason: D1 gives the zero-logical-CPU example despite available physical CPUs and states its admission-control effect.

ambiguities: A general memory-allocation speed benefit does not entail faster completion for every job.
records.claim: Disabling CUDA memory caching makes our training job finish faster than leaving caching enabled.
records.label: insufficient
records.missing_information: This job's comparable end-to-end runtimes with and without caching.
records.reason: Allocation-speed and debugging statements do not determine this particular training job's total runtime.

ambiguities: D1 is unnecessary; the claim already assumes the weights-only action and says can, not always.
records.claim: After waking only the model weights with tags=["weights"], is_sleeping can remain true until the remaining components are awake.
records.label: supported
records.reason: D3 describes weights-only wake-up and says is_sleeping stays true until all components are awake.

ambiguities: Scope is this align-mode shared-prefix checkpoint option, not every Mamba/APC feature.
records.claim: For the hybrid Mamba option described here, enabling the shared-prefix checkpoint flag is sufficient even when the model uses multi-module MTP.
records.label: contradicted
records.reason: D4 makes not using multi-module MTP a necessary condition for this checkpoint flag to take effect.

ambiguities: Pageable CPU memory in the option-scoped level-2 excerpt does not establish level-1 compression behavior.
records.claim: The level-1 CPU backup of model weights is compressed before being stored in host memory.
records.label: insufficient
records.missing_information: Whether level-1 CPU weight backups use compression.
records.reason: The packet states CPU backup but neither compressed nor uncompressed representation.

ambiguities: Both conjuncts need evidence. D1 installation context is unnecessary.
records.claim: For a cluster with different GPU types, node labels and selectors can steer a Pod to suitable nodes, and the label key does not have to be accelerator.
records.label: supported
records.reason: D3 proves node labels/selectors can route heterogeneous GPU workloads; D4 proves the key need not be accelerator.

ambiguities: Do not generalize the GPU rule to CPU or ordinary memory resources.
records.claim: For the custom GPU resource described here, setting the request to one GPU and the limit to two GPUs is permitted.
records.label: contradicted
records.reason: D2 requires equal GPU request and limit values, unlike one versus two.

ambiguities: D2 corroborates tensor/cache distinctions but D1 is sufficient.
records.claim: The documented allocated-memory functions track tensors, whereas the reserved-memory functions track the total memory managed by the caching allocator.
records.label: supported
records.reason: D1 directly distinguishes tensor-allocated from total allocator-reserved memory.

records.claim: Our current serving engine will finish waking from sleep in under five hundred milliseconds.
records.label: insufficient
records.missing_information: A wake-duration measurement or guarantee for the current engine/model/environment.
records.reason: No excerpt gives the claimed 500 ms bound.

ambiguities: The suspension rule does not imply this cluster has no free resources.
records.claim: Our cluster has enough free GPUs of type tesla to start a two-GPU job right now.
records.label: insufficient
records.missing_information: Current free tesla GPU inventory and scheduling/admission state.
records.reason: Request syntax and retention rules do not establish present availability.

ambiguities: The prohibition on changing node resource capacities after startup is a different operation and does not contradict actor migration.
records.claim: Ray can move a running GPU actor to another node without restarting that actor.
records.label: insufficient
records.missing_information: A live actor-migration/state-transfer capability and its restart requirements.
records.reason: Logical resources and device visibility do not specify whether running actors can migrate without restart.

ambiguities: Do not import an allocation heuristic from outside this packet or from a different allocator backend.
records.claim: The described PyTorch caching allocator uses first-fit selection to choose an available memory block.
records.label: insufficient
records.reason: A caching allocator and memory diagnostics do not specify first-fit selection.

ambiguities: D4 is about job steps within a job and cannot replace the suspension/other-jobs evidence.
records.claim: Suspending a job makes its allocated generic resources available for other jobs to use.
records.label: contradicted
records.reason: D2 explicitly says a suspended job's resources do not become available to other jobs.

ambiguities: Level-2 excerpts are unnecessary; restored D4 now supplies its option antecedent.
records.claim: In our proposed pause-and-resume workflow, level 1 sleep retains the existing KV-cache contents so requests resume with that unchanged cache.
records.label: contradicted
records.reason: D1 explicitly says level 1 discards and forgets the KV cache.

ambiguities: This is not hard security isolation, universal compliance, or a fixed physical GPU assignment.
records.claim: Ray provides visible-device GPU isolation by setting CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, which most machine-learning frameworks respect for assignment.
records.label: supported
records.reason: D3 explicitly describes visible-device isolation through CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES with the most-frameworks qualification.
